Commentary.Commentary: So, that wraps up the formalities of this Test. Sri Lanka will go to Colombo eyeing a whitewash and it would take a really special Australian performance to deny the hosts that pleasure. The final Test starts at the SSC on 13th August. Tune in at 1000 IST for all the action of that game. For now you can switch to the Zimbabwe-New Zealand match tab to enjoy some cricketing action. Cheers!

ANGELO MATHEWS is happy at his side beating the no.1 team and feels that Sri Lanka played outstanding cricket. Opines that the toss was crucial and is glad that he won it. A decent first innings score was vital on such a pitch and he is happy that they got a decent total. Praises Dilruwan for rising to the occasion and states they always backed the off spinner. Also lauds Starc for performing well.

STEVEN SMITH admits that it's been a tough Test from the first day itself. Opines that 281 was an above par score from SL and then accepts that his side batted too poorly in the first innings. Says that the first innings deficit cost them the game as chasing 400-plus was always going to be tough. Agrees that playing spin on such tracks is very challenging and that they have to find a way to counter it. Points to Australia's poor stats in Asia in recent times and hopes that they can turn it around.
DILRUWAN PERERA (MAN OF THE MATCH) says that he didn't do well in Pallekele but was able to find his rhythm in Galle. States that he is happy to contribute to the team's win.

With a target of 413 to win, Australia started disastrously, losing three wickets in just 6 overs before stumps on day two thereby all but sealing their own fate in the game. It was only a matter of time on the third day before the Lankans finished the game and they duly did it well inside an hour after lunch. It's the eighth successive Test defeat for Australia in Asia and plenty of problems for the tourists to ponder. Dilruwan Perera shone brightly with a fifty and 10 wickets in the match - first ever Lankan to achieve this feat.

Starc was easily the pick of the Aussie bowlers in the match. He snared a hard-working fifer in the first innings and claimed a 6-fer in the second to get a match haul of 11 wickets. Australia did threaten to fight back by picking early wickets in the Lankan second innings but the big first innings lead meant that the hosts were always just a partnership away from safety. That's what happened as K.Perera stepped in again with Mathews while Dilruwan and Dhananjaya also chipped in with handy knocks to swell the lead.

When you post just 106 in the first innings of a Test and concede a 175-run lead, you are bound to lose most of the matches. That's precisely what happened as the Australians were clueless in the first innings to the guile of Herath and Dilruwan on a track that aided the spinners in a big way. However, the surface was never unplayable as the hosts' batsmen showed in both their innings. SL got to 281 on the first day thanks to another Mendis special with help from K.Perera and skipper Mathews.

Smith and Warner started positively but once the latter departed, the innings imploded with the Aussie skipper too succumbing after getting a start. The middle and lower order hung around a bit but it was only delaying the inevitable as the visitors continued to be decimated by the spin attack from the Lankans. The Australian batsmen did use the sweep more in this innings but overall their approach continued to lack confidence.

It took only 30 minutes after the lunch break for Sri Lanka to wrap up the final 3 Australian wickets to clinch their first ever Test series victory against Australia. Dilruwan Perera took 2 of those scalps to finish with a 6-fer and a match haul of 10 wickets before Mendis' brilliance mopped up the final wicket.  The visitors started the day needing 388 more runs to win with seven wickets left and it was always going to be a difficult task on this dicey surface.

It was referred to the third umpire and the replays showed that Nevill was just short of the crease. With that, Sri Lanka win by 229 runs and seal the series!

Welcome back for the second session. Only a question of when the Lankans can wrap the 3 Aussie wickets left. How much longer can the visitors prolong the inevitable? We shall find out as the players and umpires take the field. DILRUWAN PERERA to start proceedings after lunch.
.....DAY 3, SESSION 2.....

Dilruwan Perera stole the limelight and took the prized wickets of Warner and Smith. He varied his lines, lengths and pace to perfection and also cleaned up Adam Voges to get a fifer. He has been a real star for the Sri Lankans with the ball. Sandakan was impressive in his short spell and Herath was steady with his bowling but failed to strike this time. Now it's just a matter of time before Australia get bowled out. It seems to be all done and dusted for the visitors. Join us for the post lunch session!

Sri Lanka are marching towards victory and have capitalized on the first session of day 3 impressively by taking 4 wickets.The Australians were looking up to Smith and Warner to step up a notch and play heroic knocks but that was always going to be difficult on a crumbling track and the lack of application that the Australian top order has shown throughout the series.

Floats it up on middle and leg, Warner leans into it and defends it well.
Drops it a bit short outside off, punched off the back foot to cover-point.
Floats it up on middle and leg, Smith steps out and clips it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Perera switches to around the wicket.
FOUR! SHOT! Lovely from Smith! Flighted full outside off, Smith steps out to drive it sweetly through extra cover as the ball races to the fence. Very positive start from the Aussies this morning.
Similar delivery, Smith steps down the track and hits it to mid on for a single.

FOUR! WRISTY SHOT! Tossed up around middle, Smitch dances down the track and flicks it uppishly through mid-wicket. That was timed well and the ball runs down to the boundary quickly. Good stuff from Smith!
Flighted delivery, Warner advances down the track and hits it straight down to Herath who fumbles and allows the batsmen to come through for a quick single.
Tossed up outside off, Warner looks to play it off the front foot but the ball hits the rough and turns sharpy, takes an inside edge of his bat and hits him on the pads.
FOUR! Tossed up around middle, Warner goes down on one knee and paddle sweeps it through fine leg for a crafty boundary!
Flat and shortish around middle, Warner goes deep into the crease and punches it through the covers for a couple.
Flighted on off, Smith reaches out and works it to the leg side.
Drifting away on a length outside off, Warner drives it towards deep point for a single.
Flighted on middle and off, Smith uses his feet and clips it to deep square leg for a single.
Two Leg byes! Floats up the off break on middle and leg, Smith goes across to flick but the ball goes off the pads down the leg side to fine leg. A couple of leg byes taken.
Floats it up on off, Warner looks to work across the line and gets a leading edge through the legs of silly point for a single.
FOUR! SMASHED! Warner isn't going to hold back for sure! Floats it up around off, Warner steps out to convert that into a low full toss and drills it through wide mid off for a boundary.
It shall be DILRUWAN PERERA to bowl from the other end.
Around off, spins a bit. Smith goes back and defends it confidently.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted delivery, Smith gets to the pitch of the delivery and blocks it.
FOUR! THAT'S THE FIRST BOUNDARY OF THE DAY! Flatter and shorter around middle, Smith goes back and glides it behind square leg for a well worked boundary.
Tossed up around middle, Smith advances and plays it to mid-wicket.
Floated around off, Smith leans forward and defends it solidly.

The players and umpires are out there in the middle. STEVEN SMITH and DAVID WARNER to resume their overnight stand. Crucial first session for the Australians. It shall be the wily RANGANA HERATH to start proceedings on day 3.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold feels that the track is dry and there are some cracks developing but insists that it is still decent to bat on. The Australians have more often been undone by the odd turning ball as that has affected their approach to the straighter balls. Ends by saying that the approach will be key for the tourists.

Hello and welcome to the day three coverage. Sri Lanka need 7 wickets to take an unassailable lead in the series. The Australians need another massive 388 runs to level the series and the way they have played spin this series, that looks a long, long way away. One can't help but feel that it's only a matter of time before Sri Lanka complete the formalities today. However, heroes are born from such situations. Can Australia find theirs? Stay tuned as the action isn't far away.
.....DAY 3, SESSION 1.....

That completes our coverage of an action-packed day. Tomorrow in all probability could be the final day of this match unless Australia produce a superhuman batting effort. Another 388 runs needed with 7 wickets left. No prizes for guessing who the favorites are to win from here on. Tune in at 1000 IST tomorrow for the day 3 action. Until then, it's goodbye from us.

Just 6 overs were left for the Australians to survive but they ended up losing 3 wickets in the brief period. Burns departed cheaply to Herath while D.Perera removed nightwatchman Lyon and Khawaja off successive balls. Warner attacked and Smith hung in there to prevent further damage but the writing is surely on the wall for the Australians. Their batsmen just haven't been able to adjust to the turning pitches.

Sri Lanka were rattled early in their second innings as they lost three early wickets before lunch but their middle and lower order chipped in to ensure that the lead sailed past the 400-run mark. D.Perera followed up his bowling efforts with a half-century with help from Mathews, K.Perera and de Silva. Starc was once again the star for the Aussies with a 6-wicket haul. The spinners disappointed big time for the tourists.

That completes a fast-paced day of Test match cricket with a whopping 21 wickets falling. Sri Lanka are in the driver's seat and are poised to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series. It all began in the bizarre morning session with 11 wickets falling, 8 of them Australians as the visitors slipped from 54/2 overnight to a paltry 106 all out. Herath's hat-trick was the highlight for the Lankans with him and D.Perera finishing with 4 wickets apiece.
CLOSE SHAVE FOR SMITH! Floats it up on a length on leg, Smith goes back to flick and the ball just flies past the forward short leg fielder for a brisk single. THAT SHALL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2.
Last ball of the day coming up. More close in fielders swoop in on Smith.
Flighted on middle and off, Smith steps out and drives it back to the bowler.
Flatter on middle and leg, tucked to the leg side.
Fuller on off, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller on off, David uses his feet to work it away and gets a leading edge to the off side.
Fuller on off, Warner steps out to drive and gets an inside edge on to the pads.
Last over of the day coming up.
Fullish delivery, Smith leans forward and gets beaten and the ball hits him low on the pad. There is loud appeal from the Sri Lankans but the umpire is unmoved. That looked close to the naked eye!
Warner flicks it through square leg for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Floated outside off, Warner reverse sweeps it down towards third man for a well crafted boundary! That's three boundaries on the trot for Warner!
FOUR! Outside off, Warner dances down the wicket again and drives it beautifully through the covers for a superb boundary!
FOUR! Tossed up outside off, Warner advances down the wicket and drives it down the wicket for a boundary!
Floats it up outside off, Smith steps out to that one and pushes it back to the bowler.
Fuller on off, driven firmly towards mid on. Keeps out the hat-trick ball.
STEVEN SMITH walks out to bat. He'll face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Sri Lanka are in a hurry to finish this game it seems. Slider around off, Khawaja goes forward and leaves it alone as he expects it to turn but it doesn't. Skids through after pitching to make a mess of the stumps. Golden duck for Khawaja and Perera is on a hat-trick now.
USMAN KHAWAJA walks out to bat.

OUT! PERERA STRIKES! Flighted off break outside off, Lyon lunges into it to push as the ball lobs towards silly point where Silva takes it low diving to his left. There seemed to be bat pad but the umpires aren't sure if the catch is clean. Replays show that there is faint bit of bat after the ball hit the pad first and Silva did well to take the catch cleanly as well. So, the nightwatchman departs without troubling the scorers.
Lyon seems to be caught at silly point. The umpires are checking if the catch is clean.
Slider on off, Warner plays for the turn but that one skids on off the deck. Gets a faint inside edge on to the pads and goes down the leg side for a single.
Flatter outside off, Warner tries to cut but is beaten.
Lyon presents the full face of the bat and defends it off his front foot.
Quicker one and rushes Lyon on the crease. He strides in at the last moment and does well to keep it out.
Flighted delivery around off, Lyon leans forward and defends it.
Floated outside off, holds its line. Lyon pokes at it and gets beaten.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Tossed up outside off, turns sharply. Lyon lets it go through.
Drifting away outside off, jabbed from the crease towards point.
Floats it up outside off, David gets back and blocks it out.
FOUR! CRUNCHED! Short and outside off, can't bowl there to Warner as he rocks back to slap to the deep cover fence for a boundary.
Floats it up on a length outside off, cut away to the off side.
Flatter on to the pads, Warner gets back to that one and clips it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Fuller on leg stump, Warner misses the flick and is struck on the pads.
DILRUWAN PERERA to share the new ball.
The nightwatchman NATHAN LYON walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Floated around off, Burns advances down the track and pushes it uppishly straight to Dhananjay de Silva who takes an easy catch! That was loose from Burns and he falls in the first over again in this test match. He would be kicking himself!
Flighted delivery around off, Burns gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Floated outside off, Burns steps down the wicket and pushes it through the covers for a couple.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up again in the same channel, Warner defends it hesitantly and the ball rolls off through the slip cordon and the batsmen run a single.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Warner leans forward and defends it.
